_meta.note: General adult reference ranges. Real ranges vary by lab, sex, and age. The app prefers the range printed on the uploaded report when present, and falls back to these. These ranges are NOT a diagnosis and NOT a substitute for a clinician.

analytes.name: Hemoglobin
analytes.plain: The oxygen-carrying protein inside your red blood cells.
analytes.high_means: A high value can reflect dehydration, living at altitude, smoking, or less commonly a blood disorder called polycythemia.
analytes.low_means: A low value means anemia - your blood carries less oxygen than usual. Common causes are iron deficiency, blood loss, or chronic illness.
analytes.why_matters: It is the single most common reason people feel tired and short of breath.

analytes.name: Hematocrit
analytes.plain: The percentage of your blood that is made of red blood cells.
analytes.high_means: Often tracks with hemoglobin - dehydration or altitude raise it.
analytes.low_means: A low value usually means anemia, matching a low hemoglobin.
analytes.why_matters: It is a quick check of how concentrated your red cells are.

analytes.name: White Blood Cell Count
analytes.plain: Your immune system's cells - the body's infection fighters.
analytes.high_means: A high count often means your body is fighting an infection, or reflects stress, inflammation, or steroids.
analytes.low_means: A low count can follow a viral illness, certain medicines, or a problem with the bone marrow that makes these cells.
analytes.why_matters: It is the main signal of infection and of how the immune system is doing.

analytes.name: Platelets
analytes.plain: The tiny cell fragments that let your blood clot and stop bleeding.
analytes.high_means: A high count can follow inflammation, infection, or iron deficiency.
analytes.low_means: A low count means you may bruise or bleed more easily. Causes include viral illness, medicines, or liver problems.
analytes.why_matters: It governs whether a cut will stop bleeding and whether surgery is safe.

analytes.name: Mean Corpuscular Volume
analytes.plain: The average size of your red blood cells.
analytes.high_means: Large red cells point toward vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use, or thyroid problems.
analytes.low_means: Small red cells most often mean iron deficiency or a blood condition called thalassemia.
analytes.why_matters: It tells a clinician what kind of anemia you have, which changes the treatment.

analytes.name: Glucose (Fasting)
analytes.plain: The amount of sugar in your blood after fasting.
analytes.high_means: Above 100 is prediabetes range; 126 or more on two occasions points to diabetes.
analytes.low_means: Below 70 is low blood sugar, which can cause shakiness, sweating, and confusion.
analytes.why_matters: It is the core test for diabetes, one of the most common and most treatable conditions.

analytes.name: Hemoglobin A1c
analytes.plain: Your average blood sugar over the last 2-3 months.
analytes.high_means: 5.7-6.4% is prediabetes; 6.5% or more points to diabetes; higher values mean blood sugar has run high for months.
analytes.low_means: A low value is uncommon and can reflect anemia or recent low blood sugar.
analytes.why_matters: It is the long-term report card on blood sugar, and the number used to track diabetes control.

analytes.name: Creatinine
analytes.plain: A waste product your muscles make that healthy kidneys filter out.
analytes.high_means: A high value can mean the kidneys are not filtering as well as they should, or simply dehydration.
analytes.low_means: A low value is usually harmless and can reflect low muscle mass.
analytes.why_matters: It is the main marker of kidney health.

analytes.name: Estimated GFR
analytes.plain: An estimate of how much blood your kidneys filter per minute.
analytes.high_means: A high estimate is not a concern; above 90 is normal.
analytes.low_means: Below 60 for three months or more is the definition of chronic kidney disease.
analytes.why_matters: It is the clearest single number for how well the kidneys are working.

analytes.name: Sodium
analytes.plain: A salt mineral that controls the water balance in and around your cells.
analytes.high_means: High sodium most often means dehydration or not drinking enough water.
analytes.low_means: Low sodium can come from certain medicines, heart or kidney problems, or drinking too much water.
analytes.why_matters: Sodium imbalances can cause confusion and seizures if severe.

analytes.name: Potassium
analytes.plain: A mineral that drives every heartbeat and muscle movement.
analytes.high_means: High potassium can come from kidney problems or certain blood-pressure medicines, and can affect the heart rhythm.
analytes.low_means: Low potassium often follows vomiting, diarrhea, or water pills, and can cause cramps and weakness.
analytes.why_matters: Potassium is one of the few values where an extreme result is an emergency.

analytes.name: Calcium
analytes.plain: The mineral that builds bone and runs nerve and muscle signals.
analytes.high_means: A high value can come from an overactive parathyroid gland or, rarely, cancer; it needs a clinician's eye.
analytes.low_means: Low calcium can reflect vitamin D deficiency or kidney problems.
analytes.why_matters: Calcium affects bone strength, nerves, and heart rhythm.

analytes.name: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT)
analytes.plain: A liver enzyme that leaks into the blood when liver cells are irritated.
analytes.high_means: A high value suggests the liver is inflamed - from fatty liver, alcohol, medicines, or infection.
analytes.low_means: A low value is not usually a concern.
analytes.why_matters: It is the most specific common marker of liver cell injury.

analytes.name: Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST)
analytes.plain: An enzyme found in liver and muscle; it rises when either is injured.
analytes.high_means: A high value can mean liver or muscle injury; comparing it with ALT helps tell which.
analytes.low_means: A low value is not usually a concern.
analytes.why_matters: Together with ALT it localises where an injury is coming from.

analytes.name: Total Bilirubin
analytes.plain: A yellow waste product from old red blood cells that the liver clears.
analytes.high_means: A high value can cause jaundice (yellow skin and eyes) and points to liver or bile-duct problems.
analytes.low_means: A low value is not a concern.
analytes.why_matters: It explains why jaundice appears and localises the cause.

analytes.name: Albumin
analytes.plain: The main protein your liver makes to keep fluid in your blood vessels.
analytes.high_means: A high value usually just means dehydration.
analytes.low_means: A low value can reflect liver or kidney disease, poor nutrition, or inflammation.
analytes.why_matters: It is a broad marker of liver function and overall nutrition.

analytes.name: Total Cholesterol
analytes.plain: The sum of all cholesterol in your blood.
analytes.high_means: 200-239 is borderline high and 240+ is high, which raises heart-attack and stroke risk over time.
analytes.low_means: A low value is generally not a concern.
analytes.why_matters: Cholesterol is the main modifiable driver of heart disease risk.

analytes.name: LDL Cholesterol
analytes.plain: The 'bad' cholesterol that builds up plaque inside arteries.
analytes.high_means: 100-129 is near-optimal, 130-159 borderline high, 160+ high - the higher it stays, the more plaque risk.
analytes.low_means: Lower is generally better for the heart.
analytes.why_matters: It is the single most targeted number in preventing heart attacks.

analytes.name: HDL Cholesterol
analytes.plain: The 'good' cholesterol that carries cholesterol away from arteries.
analytes.high_means: A high value is generally protective for the heart.
analytes.low_means: Below 40 (men) or 50 (women) is a heart-risk factor.
analytes.why_matters: Higher HDL is protective, so a low number is the concern here.

analytes.name: Triglycerides
analytes.plain: The form of fat that circulates in your blood after a meal.
analytes.high_means: 150-199 is borderline, 200+ is high; very high levels can inflame the pancreas.
analytes.low_means: A low value is not a concern.
analytes.why_matters: High triglycerides pair with heart risk and with fatty liver.

analytes.name: Thyroid Stimulating Hormone
analytes.plain: The hormone your brain uses to tell the thyroid how hard to work.
analytes.high_means: A high TSH usually means an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) - fatigue, weight gain, feeling cold.
analytes.low_means: A low TSH usually means an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism) - weight loss, racing heart, feeling hot.
analytes.why_matters: Thyroid problems are common, treatable, and easy to miss.

analytes.name: Vitamin D, 25-Hydroxy
analytes.plain: The vitamin your skin makes from sunlight and that keeps bones and muscles strong.
analytes.high_means: A high value is usually from too much supplementation; very high levels raise blood calcium.
analytes.low_means: Below 30 is insufficiency and below 20 is deficiency - linked to tiredness, bone aches, and low mood.
analytes.why_matters: Vitamin D deficiency is very common and cheap to correct.

analytes.name: Vitamin B12
analytes.plain: A vitamin needed to build red blood cells and keep nerves healthy.
analytes.high_means: A high value is usually from supplements and is rarely a concern by itself.
analytes.low_means: A low value causes fatigue, tingling in the hands and feet, and a form of anemia.
analytes.why_matters: Deficiency is common (especially with age or a vegan diet) and causes nerve damage if missed.

analytes.name: Ferritin
analytes.plain: The protein that stores iron - the best single test of your iron reserves.
analytes.high_means: A high value can mean iron overload, or simply inflammation or liver problems.
analytes.low_means: A low value means your iron stores are running out - the earliest sign of iron deficiency.
analytes.why_matters: It finds iron deficiency before anemia appears, which is when it is easiest to fix.

analytes.name: C-Reactive Protein
analytes.plain: A general signal of inflammation anywhere in the body.
analytes.high_means: A high value means there is inflammation somewhere - infection, injury, or a chronic condition.
analytes.low_means: A low value is normal and reassuring.
analytes.why_matters: It tells you the body is reacting, and whether a treatment is calming things down.
